data.message: Retrieving the official financial statement PDF from the CSE document repository
Document secured and staged for processing
Running multi-dimensional financial health diagnostics with LLM (this may take a minute)...
Health diagnostics finalised for KFP.N0000 — overall score: 52/100 · Fair

standardHealthChecks.name: Liquidity Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Current ratio stands at 1.21x (Current Assets of LKR 3.09B vs Current Liabilities of LKR 2.54B). However, the quick ratio is weak at 0.63x due to heavy inventory holdings, and cash reserves are dominated by substantial short-term bank overdrafts of LKR 911.9M.

standardHealthChecks.name: Profitability Health
standardHealthChecks.description: While gross margin improved slightly to 26.2%, net profit fell 27% YoY to LKR 13.6M (down from LKR 18.7M in 2025). Net profit margin is thin at 0.64%, severely compressed by rising operating and finance costs.

standardHealthChecks.name: Debt Management
standardHealthChecks.description: Total short-term borrowings and overdrafts stand at LKR 1.37B. Interest coverage ratio is tight at 1.59x (Operating Profit of LKR 44.7M vs Finance Costs of LKR 28.1M), leaving little cushion against rising interest rates.

standardHealthChecks.name: Cash Flow Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Net cash generated from operating activities improved to LKR 61.1M (up from LKR 33.2M in 2025). However, dividend outflows (LKR 68.1M) and capital expenditure (LKR 59.4M) exceeded operating cash flows, resulting in a net cash deficit of LKR 820.0M.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Inventory & Supply Chain Management
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Inventories increased by 11.4% during the quarter to LKR 1.49B, representing over 48% of total current assets. In a food processing business, high stock levels tie up liquid working capital and expose the firm to holding costs and spoilage risks.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: Essential for FMCG and food manufacturing firms to monitor perishable stock turnover, working capital lock-up, and waste/spoilage risks.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Operating Cost Efficiency
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Selling and distribution costs (+16%) and administrative expenses (+17%) grew faster than total revenue (+10%), causing operating margin to contract slightly despite gross profit expanding by 12%.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: Distribution and administrative overhead control is key to preserving operating margins in consumer food manufacturing.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Finance Cost & Interest Burden Drag
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Net finance costs jumped 64% YoY to LKR 25.3M, consuming 56.5% of operating profit (Results from operating activities).
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: High finance costs directly erode bottom-line profitability when operating margins are thin.

recommendations: Reduce reliance on expensive bank overdrafts (LKR 911.9M) by reallocating operating cash flow towards working capital stabilization and debt payoff.
Implement stricter inventory control measures to shorten the cash conversion cycle and release locked-up working capital from LKR 1.49B in stock.
Tighten control over selling, distribution, and administrative overheads, which grew faster (+16% and +17%) than top-line revenue (+10%).
Align dividend payouts more closely with free cash flow generation to avoid worsening net short-term debt positions.
result.analysisNotes: Keells Food Products PLC demonstrated steady top-line growth (+10% YoY) and healthy gross margin expansion. However, financial profitability is heavily constrained by rising administrative/distribution expenses and a 51% surge in finance costs, resulting in a 27% drop in quarterly net profit. The balance sheet exhibits significant exposure to short-term floating debt and bank overdrafts.
